---
title: Files and memory
---

A Sign keeps its content in Files, each named by a one-character File
Label. There are three types:

- A TEXT File holds a Message. The Sign shows its TEXT Files in turn.
- A STRING File holds up to 125 bytes of text that a TEXT File shows with
  `{string LABEL}`. Writing it does not blank the display.
- A DOTS PICTURE File holds a small picture that a TEXT File shows with
  `{picture LABEL}`. See [Pictures](05-pictures.qmd).

At power-up a Sign has one TEXT File, `A`. To have more, write a Memory
Configuration: the list of Files, with their types and sizes.

## Set up the Files

```python
from alpha_led_sign import DotsPictureFile, StringFile, TextFile

sign.configure_memory([
    TextFile("A", size=256),
    TextFile("B", size=256),
    StringFile("T", size=16),
    StringFile("H", size=8),
    DotsPictureFile("P", rows=7, columns=8),
])
```

::: {.callout-warning}
Writing the Memory Configuration erases every File on the Sign, TEXT File `A`
included. Do it once when you set a Sign up, then write the Files.
:::

A TEXT File's `size` is the most bytes its Message can encode to. The last File
may be a TEXT File of size 0, which takes the rest of memory. A STRING File's size
must be at least 1.

`TextFile` also takes a `run_time` (default: always) and `locked`, which stops the
File being changed from the IR keyboard. See
[Scheduling, clock, and sound](06-scheduling-clock-sound.qmd).

`sign.clear_memory()` erases every File and the Memory Configuration. It waits
1.5 s before it returns, because a 4120C read sooner still reports the old Files'
memory as in use.

### The memory budget

Every File costs its size plus 11 bytes of overhead. The library adds up a
configuration before it sends it, and warns (or raises, with `strict=True`) when
the total is more than the Sign Model's memory.

On a 4120C, measured on a real Sign:

- The memory is 28,872 bytes, not the 28,000 the brochure gives, and the Sign
  keeps 9 of them back.
- A DOTS PICTURE File costs 11 + 2 + rows × 2 × ⌈columns / 8⌉ bytes, whatever its
  color depth. The manual says pictures are not counted at all.

`SignModel.memory_needed` does the same sum, so you can check a configuration
before you send it:

```python
files = [TextFile("A", size=20_000), StringFile("T", size=16)]
models.ALPHA_4120C.memory_needed(files)    # 20047
```

A Sign refuses a configuration that does not fit, and keeps its old Files.

## Live values: STRING Files

Writing a TEXT File blanks the display while the Sign takes the new content.
Writing a STRING File does not, so STRING Files are the way to show values that
change: a temperature, a score, a queue length.

Put a `{string LABEL}` in a TEXT File once, then write only the STRING File:

```python
sign.write_text("A", "{color amber}Temp: {color green}{string T}")

while True:
    sign.write_string("T", f"{read_sensor():.1f}F")
    time.sleep(10)
```

STRING File content is literal text and a few Control Codes. It can hold colors
(except the two rainbow colors), fonts, speeds, spacing, wide characters, the time,
and `{new_line}`. It can't hold Frames or other Control Codes; the library raises
`ValueError` before it sends one. Content longer than 125 bytes also raises.

Write at most the File's size. A 4120C given more than a STRING File's size emptied
the File and recorded an error.

## The Priority TEXT File

The Priority TEXT File replaces everything on the display until it is cleared:

```python
sign.priority("{frame flash}{color red}EVACUATE")
...
sign.clear_priority()
```

It holds at most 125 bytes, and needs no Memory Configuration. Writing Run Times
or Run Days also ends it.

## Reading Files back

```python
sign.read_text("A")      # a Message
sign.read_string("T")    # a tuple of Segments, such as ('72.5F',)
```

See [Reading back and discovery](07-reading-and-discovery.qmd) for what reads need.
